name: Pediatric lateral approach to the distal humerus
corridor: Between brachioradialis and triceps proximally, continuing anterior to anconeus along the posterior border of the extensor mass

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on radiolucent support, elbow freely mobile, and imaging available for AP, lateral, oblique, and arthrogram assessment.

setup.text: Plan fixation and arthrogram use while prioritizing preservation of the posterolateral soft-tissue attachments that supply the fragment.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark lateral supracondylar ridge, lateral epicondyle, capitellum, radial head, proximal radius, and olecranon.

incision.text: Begin 3-5 cm above the joint on the lateral ridge and extend posterior to the radial head onto proximal forearm; place it slightly more posterior than the adult incision.

superficial_interval.text: Open fascia on the lateral ridge and develop the interval between brachioradialis and triceps, continuing anterior to anconeus.

deep_interval.text: Open capsule anteriorly over capitellum toward radial head; elevate only the anterior tissue needed for visualization and preserve posterior fragment attachments.

layers.text: Skin, lateral fascia, brachioradialis-triceps interval, extensor/anconeus border, capsule, then capitellum and lateral condyle.

structures_encountered.text: Brachioradialis, triceps, extensor origin, anconeus, capsule, capitellum, radial head, and lateral-condyle fragment are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Radial nerve and its branches near radial head, posterior fragment vascularity, articular cartilage, physis, and lateral collateral ligament are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Do not strip the posterolateral fragment attachments and do not place a lever retractor anteriorly near the radial nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Use smooth soft-tissue retraction; anterior levering risks radial nerve injury and posterior stripping risks fragment devascularization.

exposure.text: Exposes lateral condyle, capitellum, radiocapitellar joint, and anterior articular surface for direct reduction.

limitations.text: The approach does not expose the medial column and aggressive posterior extension threatens fragment blood supply.

extensions.text: Release anterior capsule or limited anterior brachioradialis/ECRL and posterior triceps attachments only as required for visualization.

indications.text: Use for displaced lateral-condyle or capitellar fractures, unstable lateral-ligament avulsion, and selected irreducible supracondylar fractures.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid unnecessary open exposure when closed reduction provides congruent stable alignment and avoid this isolated corridor for medial or bicondylar pathology.

implant_implications.text: Select wire or screw trajectories that stabilize the fragment without violating the joint, physis, or preserved posterior vascular attachments.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm articular congruity and fixation on AP, lateral, internal-oblique views and use arthrography when the cartilaginous surface is not directly visible.

closure.text: Repair capsule, muscle-fascial interval, and skin with absorbable sutures without strangulating preserved posterior tissues.

complications.text: Complications include nonunion, malunion, lateral overgrowth, fishtail deformity, growth arrest, stiffness, infection, radial neuropathy, and osteonecrosis.

bailouts.text: If the joint surface cannot be judged, use arthrogram and limited capsular extension rather than circumferential fragment stripping.

procedure_applications.condition: A displaced or incongruent lateral-condyle fracture requires open articular reduction
A displaced capitellar fracture requires direct lateral access

questions.question: Which attachments protect fragment blood supply?
questions.answer: The posterior and posterolateral soft-tissue attachments.

questions.question: Which nerve is endangered near radial head?
questions.answer: The radial nerve as it divides into superficial and deep branches.

questions.question: Which view best profiles lateral-condyle displacement?
